posts.title: A trip to Suffolk August 2026
posts.description: Our first non-dog related comfort break stop was at the picnic site on the River Stour at Cattawade. The attraction being a long-staying moulting male Hudsonian Godwit on a tidal basin. As soon as we arrived I located it with Black-tailed Godwits feeding in a channel, with the receding tide it moved to another more distant channel, it shadowed a Black-tailed Godwit so I got to enjoy all the flight features. We also saw Common Sandpiper, Greenshank and Redshanks and Lapwings as well as Teal and Shelducks here. We visited the nearby National Trust managed Flatford Mill for a shady stroll in ‘Constable Country’ and enjoy a lunch on the bank of the Stour. Our next stop was Sutton Hoo to explore this interesting area and take in the historical exhibitions. Following this we headed to where we were to stay for the night, the Bell Inn at Walberswick. posts.title: Sierra Norte, Sevilla Province, Andalucia with stops and overnight stays in Malaga Province 26-31 July 2026
posts.description: 26 July- A late arrival in Malaga, no issues with flight or car hire and on to stay at our usual hostal in Casabermeja. Only camera and binoculars for this trip as we travelled light. 27 July- I was up and out early, a twenty minute drive to Rio de la Cueva bridge near Riogordo to look for Rufous-tailed Scrub Robin, perhaps a little late in the season and little time but worth a go. No luck with this species but plenty of other species and great views including Bee Eater, Kestrel, Spotted Flycatchers, Woodchats, Western Orphean Warblers, Golden Oriole (pictured). Golden Oriole and Western Orphean Warblers A good breakfast in Casabermeja and on the road for Seville province, although not far, a stop at Laguna de Fuente de Piedra was welcome, good to see some water and lots of birds. posts.title: Summer 2025 highlights
posts.description: July has been an interesting month for local sightings. A flock of Common Scoters were hard to count in the choppy ebb tide waters of the Severn on 17 July, it turned out to total 27 (7 females), I managed a minimum count of 25 (5 females) as the drifted out, often being harassed by gulls causing them to dive. A Wood Sandpiper on the Rushy at WWT Slimbridge was a welcome sighting. Whinchats Pictured below) have begun to turn up locally along with a wide range of adult and juvenile waders on the Severn and WWT scrapes. The water levels are low so Grey Herons, Little and Great Egrets (pictured on Tack Piece) are all concentrating where the fishing is productive. The Severn has been attracting numbers, typically on the ebb tide. Pick of the birds locally has been the family party of Bearded Tits, I repeatedly missed them of late with my last encounter in November last year, although there has been sightings over the winter and especially recently.
